verdicts.reason: Same correct unit economics, but Output 2 adds sharper diagnosis (Women Body Razor converts 3.3% so the audience fails, not the product), flags the current over-budget run rate, and adds COD-specific rules like refusals by ad set and cleaning refused buyers from the lookalike seed.

Both share the right $27.10 / $38 math and phasing; Output 2 is more hand-off ready with owners and done-when checks, a launch gate, marginal-CPA rule after raises and disclosure/AI-label rules, though its learning-phase figure is understated.

Output 1 delivers launch-ready concepts with headlines, character counts, safe zones, extra hooks and a concrete keep/cut rule, while Output 2 is thinner and its cost-per-trip ad edges toward an unapproved durability implication.
Output 1 has stronger angles (blind sip), hooks mapped to awareness, early spoken disclosure and a full creator brief with deliverables, dates, rights and pay, which Output 2 lacks.
Both copy sets fit limits and approved claims; Output 2 adds a usable keep/cut rule, a clever brand-name angle and the FSSAI and dates-natural-sugar caution.
Near-identical approach, but Output 2 builds in a note-count placeholder in specs and FAQ plus a link to full-note wallets that keeps wrong-fit buyers shopping, and a fallback if conversion drops.
Output 2 shows deeper Klaviyo craft (unique coupon tag, checkout pause, smart sending, subject A/B) and a more useful interactive WhatsApp help message, though it invents a shorter 7-day code expiry.

Both have holdouts and checked value maths; Output 2 shows better retention judgment with an always-on day-68 flow, offers only at message 3, value/discount-history segments, complaint fix-first and re-permission for the over-365 group.

Output 1 ties every move to contribution margin as a share of revenue (13.6% to 7.8%, $10 CPA = 2.9 pts), which is exactly the board's goal, while Output 2's per-1,000 sizing is harder to rank and its ceiling example ignores repeat value.

Both maths check out; Output 2 adds cannibalisation break-even for the duo, a Pick Any 2 for sub-499 buyers, a free-gift kit with the ad-code caveat and a compared ₹849 alternative, though its pre/post threshold test is weaker than Output 1's split.

Both have correct MDE maths; Output 2 judges every test on orders, uses delivered orders for the COD test and handles trial returns and AOV guardrails, while Output 1 relies on add-to-cart for three tests despite a smart 2x2 design.

Output 2 is more submission-ready (headers, samples, cancellation and missed-delivery templates), sizes the prepaid nudge against post-confirmation RTO, skips trusted COD buyers, caps agent call capacity and adds a cart holdout.
